paragraphs: Friend, Paul had a whole room of powerful people and every reason to protect himself. Instead, he told them about the worst thing he ever did. He said he put many of the saints in prison and went to foreign cities in "raging fury" against them (Acts 26:10-11). Then he told them who stopped him: Jesus, who said, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting" (Acts 26:15).

Here's what that teaches me. Paul didn't hide his past, because his story was never about how good he was. It was about what Jesus did. Jesus told him He was sending him "to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light" and receive "forgiveness of sins" (Acts 26:18). I know a little about being found in the dark, friend, and it is the best news there is.

Look at how it ends, too. Paul doesn't ask the king for a favor. He says, "I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains" (Acts 26:29). The man in the chains was the one hoping for the people in the nice chairs! So when you tell somebody what Jesus has done for you, tell it straight, tell it kindly, and hope good things for whoever is listening. This story isn't over, either, because Paul said he appealed to Caesar and that decision is still ahead of him.
